added_models.model: ASP6294 (PEG-Fab') vs anti-NGF IgG in adjuvant-arthritis mice and MIA-arthritis rats

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text searched (PMC9721442): no bladder or cystitis model. model_first_use_year 2016 is a proxy from the IC trial's EudraCT number (2016-004138-12); the paper is dated later.
efficacy.note: ASP6294 (PEGylated Fab') relieved pain in adjuvant-arthritis mice and MIA-arthritis rats like an anti-NGF IgG; no bladder model reported.
efficacy.quote: The anti-NGF PEGylated Fab' showed specific binding to and biological inhibitory activity against NGF, and analgesic effects in adjuvant-induced arthritis model mice in a similar manner to an anti-NGF IgG.
efficacy.judgement: ASP6294 went into IC patients on Astellas's own arthritis pain models, not the draft's NGF-sequestration cystitis models, so it is its own track; prediction is class-level analgesia.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign of pain change vs control (rodent arthritis pain vs IC/BPS daily pain NRS)
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record read (results first posted 2020-02-08); the model paper was public 2022-12-02 (PMC release), which dates the pairing.
efficacy.note: ASP6294 320 mg SC every 4 weeks did not beat placebo on the primary pain endpoint in IC/BPS (LS mean -0.2, P=0.591).
efficacy.quote: Analysis type superiority P-value = 0.591 Method MMRM Parameter type Least-Squares (LS) Mean Difference Point estimate -0.2
efficacy.judgement: Paired by us: Koya 2023 reports only that ASP6294 was well tolerated in IC/BPS, not the efficacy miss. Not a retrodiction: the rodent work selected the candidate before the trial, though published after it. Dated 2022, when both sides were public.

safety.confidence_note: Full text searched. model_first_use_year 2016 is a proxy (EudraCT 2016-004138-12).
safety.note: In MIA-arthritis rats an anti-NGF IgG promoted joint edema over time and ASP6294 did not; a lower joint-harm risk was predicted.
safety.quote: While the anti-NGF IgG promoted edema over time, the anti-NGF PEGylated Fab' did not.
safety.judgement: A different safety system from the draft's three-species toxicology: an IgG-vs-Fab' joint-edema comparison in arthritic rats, designed against the class's RPOA signal.

safety.magnitude_basis: presence vs absence of joint or serious adverse events
safety.confidence_note: Sponsor authors; the statement is global, not joint-specific, and a 12-week trial in ~56 dosed women without OA can barely show RPOA. EU CTR record lists 0/56 SAEs on ASP6294.
safety.note: Sponsor reports ASP6294 well tolerated and safe in IC/BPS; registry shows 0/56 serious adverse events on drug vs 3/61 on placebo.
safety.short: ASP6294 safe in IC/BPS as predicted
safety.quote: Phase 1 and Phase 2a clinical studies of anti-NGF Fab’-PEG (ASP6294) have been completed, and ASP6294 was well-tolerated and safe in healthy subjects and subjects with bladder pain syndrome/interstitial cystitis.
safety.reason: No harm seen; trial too small for RPOA
safety.judgement: Scored same because the model's stated prediction (lower adverse-effect risk than IgG) was not contradicted, but the comparison has little power to contradict it; hence low confidence.

added_models.model: Rat medial meniscal tear model dosed with tanezumab

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. First use dated by publication (epub 2016-07-05); the experiments are undated.
safety.note: Rat medial meniscal tear model dosed with tanezumab, built to test whether it reproduces the RPOA seen in OA trials.
safety.short: Rat MMT built to model RPOA
safety.quote: To investigate whether the effects of nerve growth factor (NGF) inhibition with tanezumab on rats with medial meniscal tear (MMT) effectively model rapidly progressive osteoarthritis (RPOA) observed in clinical trials.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for a model run after the clinical joint harm was known (2010 hold).

safety.magnitude_basis: presence of cartilage damage vs patient RPOA; bone response not reproduced
safety.note: Early tanezumab let rats load the injured joint and worsened cartilage damage, but the model missed the hypotrophic bone response of patient RPOA.
safety.short: Reproduces cartilage, not bone, of RPOA
safety.quote: This model failed to replicate the hypotrophic bone response observed in tanezumab-treated patients with RPOA.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: RPOA in OA trials was known from 2010. Reproduced cartilage damage (more severe with prophylactic tanezumab) but not the bone phenotype, so retro with source_calls_it partial. Safety imported from OA (MONDO:0005178).

considered_not_added: Rabbit ACLT/meniscectomy OA with anti-NGF (Menges 2023, doi:10.3389/fphys.2023.1201328): a non-member Merck antibody, and the paper only says its findings may help understand RPOA; it states no comparison of its structural results with patients.
Mouse recurrent-UTI bladder pain with NGF-neutralizing antibody (Hayes 2024, doi:10.1126/sciimmunol.adi5578): rUTI not IC, non-member antibody, no comparison with the anti-NGF IC trials.
Tanezumab TMDD / free-NGF model (Shoji 2023, doi:10.1002/psp4.13015): fitted to OA patient data at 2.5/5 mg SC; not a preclinical prediction and not used for IC dosing.
Tanezumab dose-response modelling of WOMAC pain (PMID 40566820): OA efficacy only, fitted to Phase 3 data.

Mouse CYP cystitis with neurotrophin-receptor inhibition (doi:10.3389/fruro.2022.1037511) and TrkA inhibition in CYP cystitis (PMID 37275761): non-member mechanisms (receptor inhibitors) and no patient comparison; same system as the draft's chemical-cystitis track.
Fulranumab-specific preclinical models: none found in Europe PMC; Wang 2017 (fulranumab IC trial) belongs in the draft's existing efficacy patient_trials, not a new track.
Urinary NGF as a responder biomarker for anti-NGF in IC/BPS: no source testing it against trial response found.
ASP6294 placental-transfer studies in pregnant rats and primates (Koya 2023): no patient comparison possible (no pregnancies reported).
